key_insight: PIKS extends kernel learning to physics-informed settings and is proven to converge universally under linear differential constraints, even when the true solution is outside the RKHS.
engineering_relevance: It offers a theoretically grounded surrogate modeling option for solid mechanics and other PDE-based engineering problems, with closed-form solutions and competitive performance against PINNs and FEM.
method: Impose linear differential constraints directly in a kernel learning framework
Use universal kernels such as Gaussian or Matérn to ensure asymptotic consistency
Derive finite-sample guarantees via operator-theoretic analysis and source conditions
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical experiments showing PIKS can be competitive with PINNs and traditional finite element methods.
watch_item: Performance guarantees rely on linear constraints and suitable source conditions, so practical accuracy may depend on kernel choice and problem regularity.
